findings.title: Unlocked read of b.cache in TotalDocs causes a concurrent map read/write panic
findings.body: `TotalDocs()` iterates over `b.cache` without acquiring `b.cacheMu.RLock()`. With `BuildIndex` now only locking around `b.cache[key] = idx` (and `getOrCreateIndex` being called from concurrent `Search` and watch-event handlers), calling `TotalDocs()` while another goroutine builds and inserts an index will trigger a fatal concurrent map iteration and map write panic.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows concurrent builds of the same key to collide on disk or leak indices
findings.body: Previously `BuildIndex` held `b.cacheMu` for the entire build. Now it only locks when assigning `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end, and `searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex` has no per-key synchronization. If two callers (e.g., concurrent `Search` requests or watch events for an unindexed namespace) miss the cache in `GetIndex` at the same time, both will run `BuildIndex` for the same `NamespacedResource`: for file-backed indices (`size > b.opts.FileThreshold`), the second `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` fails because the directory/BoltDB file already exists; for memory indices, one index overwrites the other in `b.cache` and `IndexTenants` metrics are double-incremented.

findings.title: If NewResourceServer fails during s.Init(ctx), the cancelable server context and any started background routines are leaked
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` creates `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(...)` on line 229 and now calls `s.Init(ctx)` on line 258. If `s.Init(ctx)` returns an error (for example in `s.search.init` or `s.initWatcher`), `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `cancel()` or stopping `s.lifecycle`, leaking the context and any background goroutines started during partial initialization.

findings.title: Removing s.Init checks from RPC handlers allows requests to proceed after Stop() is called
findings.body: `Stop()` sets `s.initErr = fmt.Errorf("service is stopping")` / `"service is stopped"` to reject subsequent requests via `s.Init(ctx)`, which returns `s.initErr`. Removing the `if err := s.Init(ctx); err != nil` checks from `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Read`, `List`, `Watch`, `Search`, `History`, `Origin`, `IsHealthy`, `PutBlob`, and `GetBlob` means `s.initErr` is no longer consulted by any RPC handler, so calls made while or after the server stops will no longer be rejected.
